evidence: Cic. Div. 2.141: cāsū nōnnumquam forte temere concurrerent (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Blindly, without design: things that happen forte temere, by mere chance, or that are done at random. Its commonest sense is “rashly” (cavētō aliēnam disciplīnam temere contemnās, Cato Agr. 1.4).

evidence: Cic. Top. 73: concursiō rērum fortuītārum (Lewis & Short)
Cic. de Or. 1.150: subita et fortuīta ōrātiō (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of what happens by chance, a chance meeting, an unplanned speech; not of a thing picked at random.

terms.gloss: any at all, a random one
evidence: Cic. Rosc. Am. 8: quaelibet minima rēs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: For “pick a random one”: “any one you like, the first that comes”.

phrases.latin: quam saepe forte temere ēveniunt, quae nōn audeās optāre!
phrases.english: how often things happen by mere chance that you wouldn’t dare to wish for!

temere.html: A petrified locative of an s-stem noun *temes- “darkness” (Proto-Italic *temesi), whose ending gives a short -e: “in the dark”, so “blindly” (de Vaan 609, s.v. temere).

fortuitus.against: Lewis & Short marks the vowel common
fortuitus.html: Long in Hor. C. 2.15.17 and Phaedr. 2.4.4, short only in Petronius, Juvenal and Manilius (Lewis & Short, s.v.); the classical scansion is long.

sources: Lewis & Short: temere · Lewis & Short: fortuitus · Lewis & Short: quilibet
